title: A direct-image test for tensor vanishing under an open immersion
statement: Let $j:Y\to X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], let $G$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $i\in\mathbf Z$. If $H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}j_*G)=0$ in the K-flat-model sense [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes], then $H^i(R(E)\otimes^{\mathbf L}G)=0$, where $R$ is the functor on derived categories induced by exact module restriction along $j$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. The source and target derived categories may use independent localization universes. No quasi-coherence or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08DX, lemma-quasi-coherence-tensor-product, proof of (1), locality of the derived tensor calculation; cohomology.tex Tag 06YC, lemma-pullback-K-flat

proof.text: Unpack the K-flat representative C and representing isomorphism in the hypothesis. Tensor pullback preserves K-flatness by the pullback preservation theorem. Identify tensor pullback with restriction R by uniqueness of left adjoints to j_*. Transport K-flatness along the termwise isomorphism, using functoriality of total tensor. The exact-functor localization comparison gives Q(R(C)) isomorphic to R(E), even with independent localization universes.

Transport the proved strong monoidal structure of module pullback to R through restrictFunctorIsoPullback. Compose its inverse tensorator R(F tensor j_*G) ≅ R(F) tensor R(j_*G) with the open-immersion counit R(j_*G) ≅ G. Naturality of the inverse tensorator and whisker exchange prove naturality in F. This yields a natural isomorphism tensorRight(j_*G) followed by R ≅ R followed by tensorRight(G).

Use the proved source-library CochainComplex.mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso (WeilConjectures.FromJoel.Algebra.Homology.BifunctorSingle, lines 137–141) to identify tensor with a degree-zero sheaf with termwise tensor. Map the natural isomorphism of the preceding step to complexes by NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex. Compose with the two bifunctor-single comparisons to identify R(C tensor j_*G[0]) with R(C) tensor G[0]. Exact restriction preserves zero objects and commutes with homology by Functor.mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso. Apply these to the hypothesis and transport through the complex isomorphism. Together with the K-flatness and representing isomorphism of step 1 this supplies the conclusion.

theorem openImmersion_tensor_vanishing_test {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (j : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (i : ℤ)
    (h : schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes X E ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward j).obj G) i) :
    let R : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor j
    letI : R.Additive := ⟨by intros; rfl⟩
    letI : PreservesFiniteLimits R := by
      dsimp [R, Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor]
      infer_instance
    letI : PreservesFiniteColimits R := by
      let H : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) ⥤
          SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) := Scheme.Modules.pushforward j
      have adj : R ⊣ H := Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction j
      have : R.IsLeftAdjoint := adj.isLeftAdjoint
      infer_instance
    schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes Y (R.mapDerivedCategory.obj E) G i
